context: Trim ~88+ bytes from the active instruction surface (AGENTS.md and the CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md/ANTIGRAVITY.md adapters) or raise the budget deliberately with a recorded justification. Prefer trimming: the budget exists to keep the always-loaded instruction surface small. Separately, make the hook's failure message name the actual failing check, since 'reject stale agent Git identity' pointed at the wrong cause.
description: As of develop@916d9533ab the pre-commit hook 'reject stale agent Git identity' (hook id agent-git-identity, which runs make agent-identity-check) FAILS on a clean checkout with: 'ERROR: active instruction bytes 16088 exceed budget 16000' (active_bytes=16088, agents_lines=167). Because it is a pre-commit hook rather than a CI-only gate, this blocks EVERY commit in every worktree until the instruction files are trimmed back under budget. Verified on a pristine 'git reset --hard origin/develop' with no local changes, so it is not caused by any in-flight branch. The immediately preceding commit is 916d9533ab 'docs(agents): record that the agent-identity instruction is external (#1541)', which added instruction prose - the overshoot is 88 bytes. Note the hook's NAME is misleading: it reports a stale-agent-identity failure while the actual cause is the instruction byte budget, which cost real diagnosis time.

preserves.behavior: The instruction-byte budget stays enforced; do not simply delete the gate

verifications.description: the agent instruction audit passes on a clean tree
verifications.expected: Exits 0 once active bytes are under budget

work_units.summary: Bring active instruction bytes back under budget
Make the hook report the check that actually failed
